title: Harassment vs. Terroristic Threats
summary: Annoying or alarming conduct vs. a threat meant to terrorize.

rows.label: What was said or done
cells: Annoying or alarming communications, offensive touching or a threat to touch, a course of alarming conduct
A threat to commit a crime of violence, or a threat to kill

rows.label: Purpose
cells: To harass, or to alarm or seriously annoy
To terrorize or cause evacuation; or to put the victim in imminent fear of death

rows.label: Victim's belief
cells: For a threat to kill, circumstances must make the victim reasonably believe it

rows.label: Grade
cells: Petty disorderly; 4th° in some cases (for example, on parole or probation)

tip: Write the threat in the suspect's exact words, plus the setting and the victim's reaction. Context decides which charge fits.
note: Plain-language summary. Not yet verified against official sources. Read the full statute before charging.
